questions.title: How does the fastText-based classifier improve over successive iterations in the DeepSeekMath data collection pipeline?
questions.question_body: The paper describes an iterative process where a fastText model is initially trained on 500k positive and 500k negative examples from OpenWebMath, then used to recall more math pages from Common Crawl. After four iterations, only 120B tokens remain. I am confused about how the training data for the fastText classifier is expanded in each iteration and what criteria are used to select *new* positive examples. Does the classifier simply rely on previously collected domains that have at least 10% coverage, or are there additional heuristics? Also, how does the ranking of pages by the classifier scores influence the final token count?

questions.title: Why do arXiv papers fail to improve mathematical reasoning in DeepSeekMath?
questions.question_body: The authors claim that training on arXiv data—either MathPile (mostly arXiv papers) or ArXiv-RedPajama—does not improve performance on GSM8K, MATH, MMLU-STEM, or miniF2F. I know arXiv contains formal mathematics, but I cannot see why it would be ineffective. Was it simply because the corpora were not cleaned enough? Or is there evidence that the style or vocabulary of arXiv papers is too dissimilar from the evaluation datasets? Could this result be a consequence of limited model capacity (1.3B vs 7B)?
